run: 2026-11-13 release gate over 3edd0b1..2d09df2, run by a separate overnight session (fleet ledger D1160), Opus 5.5 at xhigh; findings copied verbatim, the rest transcribed from its report
verdictLine: PASS WITH FOLLOW-UPS: no blocking finding; re-ran everything at 2d09df2

findings.summary: The speed guards still fail the engine suite under sustained load, retry included: with parallel gates running (load average about 230), 2 of 5 runs of the full engine suite failed one guard each, and gate-kit refused its baseline for that reason. tests/README.md:46 says a slow machine does not fail them; 979b87b says a burst no longer does. The retry covers a burst during one measurement, not load that spans both.
findings.repro: With two `gate-kit mutants --jobs 4` runs going elsewhere on the box (load average 230 at 22:38), run `php tests/engine/run.php` 5× in a copy of HEAD 2d09df2: run 1 `FAIL perf guard: a possessive paragraph 4× as long takes under 8× as long (10.4×: 4.4 → 46.1 ms)`, run 2 `FAIL perf guard: honorifics with and without a period 4× as long takes under 8× as long (9.6×: 8.9 → 85.5 ms)`, runs 3–5 green. `gate-kit mutants <spec> --brief -- php tests/engine/run.php` printed `refuse fails unmutated (exit 1)  baseline`.
findings.acceptance: 10 consecutive full engine runs are green while a `gate-kit mutants --jobs 4` runs on the same box, and the inSpans linear-walk mutant (M30) still fails both new path guards at about 14–16×.
findings.fix: Measure more than twice while over the limit (for example up to 3 retries, keeping the minimum), or size the small page of each guard so it takes 20 ms or more (the failing ones measure 4–9 ms, where scheduler noise dominates). Or say in tests/README.md that heavy parallel load can still fail them.
findings.cause: Each measurement is best of 3 on pages of a few milliseconds; sustained overload skews both the first and the retried measurement.

findings.location: README.md:388-400 (## Performance; the 8.2 row at :396 gives the dense page 5.0 ms)
findings.summary: The README says the 100 KB dense page meets the 5 ms budget on PHP 8.2 with no margin (table 5.0 ms at :396, a gate median of 4.87 ms at :400, measured 2026-11-05). The delta adds urlSpans work to two default-on rules (dashes, ellipsis) and makes the dense page 3–7% slower, so at HEAD the 8.2 dense median is probably 5.0–5.2 ms, over the budget the README says is met.
findings.repro: Interleaved `php -d opcache.enable_cli=1 -d opcache.jit=off tests/engine/perf.php 300`, HEAD 2d09df2 against base 3edd0b1 (git archive). Dense-page minimums, native PHP 8.5.12: HEAD 5.30/5.12/5.21 ms, base 5.13/4.94/4.94 ms (+3–5%). php8.2 in the DDEV container: HEAD 6.24/6.37/6.34 ms, base 5.85/6.17/6.14 ms (+3–7%). Typical article unchanged. The box was under load (average 47–230), so the absolute numbers are inflated; only the ratio holds.
findings.acceptance: perf.php re-run at HEAD on a quiet machine under PHP 8.2 in php:8.2-cli, and README.md:392-400 updated to the measured medians, with the budget sentence true as written, or a note that the dense page now sits at or just over it.
findings.fix: Re-measure and update the table and the budget sentence. If the dense page must stay under 5 ms, compute urlSpans once per run and share it between DashesRule and EllipsisRule (each computes it today).
findings.cause: c483cc3/8cf7af5 put urlSpans() in two default-on rules; each calls it once per run that holds a / or www.

findings.summary: ‟ (U+201F) and ‛ (U+201B) do not open a path, so a path after either is converted, though README.md:374 says the curly marks open a path, and HookQuotesRule (lines 38, 51) treats both as opening quotation marks. QuoteScanner does not read them, and no rule or locale writes them.
findings.acceptance: Either the look-behind accepts \xE2\x80\x9F and \xE2\x80\x9B, with a corpus case (`‟/var/a--b”` and `‛/var/c--d’` unchanged), or README.md:374 names the marks it accepts (“ ” ‘ ’ „ ‚ « » ‹ ›) and lists ‟ ‛ under what is not recognised.
findings.fix: Add `|\xE2\x80\x9F|\xE2\x80\x9B` to the look-behind alternation and one corpus case, or reword the README sentence.
findings.cause: The look-behind lists the marks QuoteScanner writes; HookQuotesRule's wider set was not considered.

findings.summary: The README calls U+2009 a no-break space: “A no-break space (U+00A0, U+202F, U+2009 or ` `) opens a path but does not end a URL or a path”. U+2009 THIN SPACE is a breaking space. The behaviour is as written (it opens a path and does not end one); only the label is wrong, in a typography product.
findings.repro: Static: README.md:374, the sentence quoted above.
findings.acceptance: The sentence names U+2009 as a thin space, for example: “A no-break space (U+00A0, U+202F or ` `) or a thin space (U+2009) opens a path but does not end one”.
findings.cause: The list follows the look-behind's alternation, which groups the thin space with the no-break spaces.

findings.location: pre-existing, not in the delta: rule order (ranges 50 before primes 70; locale spacing 110 after the ellipsis rules); README.md:369 (second-pass Known limit)
findings.summary: Pre-existing, outside the delta: with the Bringhurst preset or the styling hooks on, machine-made inputs change on a second pass in every locale, while README.md:369 names only apostrophes or primes switched off (the default rules: none). The delta makes this better, not worse: across 4 seeds × 3,000 inputs × 16 locales × 4 rule sets (768,000 runs), HEAD has no second-pass change that base 3edd0b1 lacks, and fixes 860 that base had. The default rule set had 0 at HEAD.

findings.location: tests/*-test.php (no URL or path case; the one `a--b` URL in page-pass-test.php:99 is an og:url attribute)
findings.summary: No Craft-layer suite pins the URL and path guard end to end, though the fix round's F1 is about the form Twig and the filter hand the engine (`"`, `'`). It works: a read-only probe in the testbed (Lite, defaults) rendered `{{ v|sorts }}` and `{% apply sorts %}` of `"/var/log/a--b" and '/tmp/x...y' then "quoted"--done...` as `“/var/log/a--b” and ‘/tmp/x...y’ then “quoted”—done…`, and `Visit https://example.com/a--b... or www.example.com/c...d -- ok` with the URLs intact. But nothing fails if the Craft layer ever changes how it escapes.
findings.acceptance: twig-test.php checks that `{{ v|sorts }}` with v = `"/var/a--b" and https://example.com/c...d` gives `“/var/a--b” and https://example.com/c...d`, and the check goes red when AbstractRule's `"` and `'` look-behinds are dropped.
findings.fix: One twig-test check (and, optionally, one page-pass check on a Pro page with an entry title holding a path).
findings.cause: The delta's tests are all engine corpus cases.
